title: Freeze a permissions table

blocks.text: The authorizer builds one `AccessPolicy` at startup from a table the config loader produces, and asks it on every request. Last week an auditor exported customer data the policy had never granted. The loader reuses its lists when it reloads, and a plugin ships a class that extends `AccessPolicy`.

Finish `src/main/java/practice/AccessPolicy.java` so that a policy, once built, answers the same for as long as it lives: whatever its caller later does with the map and lists it passed in, or with what `actionsFor` and `roles` return, and whatever class a caller passes off as an `AccessPolicy`. Requests for a role or an action the table doesn't give are still refused, and `actionsFor` keeps the order the table gave.
About five lines in total, in `frozenCopy` and the class declaration.

cases.says: the policy allows exactly the actions its table gives each role, and nothing for a role it doesn't know
actionsFor lists a role's actions in the order they were given, and is empty for an unknown role
changing the lists the policy was built from afterwards doesn't change its answers
adding to the list actionsFor returns doesn't give a role a new action
removing from the set roles returns doesn't take a role out of the policy
no subclass can override how a policy answers

origin.section: An Immutable Class Is final, and Copies Every Mutable Part, Not Just the Collection

concepts: A final field holds a reference; a class is immutable only as deep as its copy, so mutable elements are copied too or replaced by immutable ones.
Final fields and no setters don't make a type immutable while it can be subclassed; the class is final, or has only private constructors.
